The relation is inferred coherence across skill areas (emergent reading to oral narrative), not a mandatory prerequisite; lexical overlap alone ('pictures', 'story') was not treated as sufficient. This is meaningful cross-skill-area coherence and mutual reinforcement through a common classroom activity, so a symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment rather than a developmental buildsTowards (which term order would otherwise permit only first_to_second). judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade R (rank 0), Term 3, Skill Area 'EMERGENT WRITING', but under different printed sub-strands: 'Works with words' (first: 'Contributes sentences to a class piece of writing: child dictates as the teacher writes') and 'Emergent Writing:' (second: 'Uses writing tools with greater confidence and ease: crayons and pencils'). They address complementary facets of emergent writing — oral composition/authorship through shared dictated writing versus growing physical control and confidence with crayons and pencils. Neither statement's evidence shows that proficiency in one supports success in the other: dictating sentences explicitly offloads transcription to the teacher, and increased tool ease is a fine-motor advance independent of sentence composition. Shared skill area, same term, page 51 proximity and the 'writing'/'emergent' token overlap are coherence signals only, not developmental dependency, and same-rank, same-term placement gives no directional evidence. Substantive conceptual coherence within emergent writing therefore supports relatesTo rather than buildsTowards. Note that both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and the first endpoint's LC evidence is truncated, so unseen text could exist; the visible statements are nonetheless unambiguous enough for this symmetric judgment.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade R (rank 0) Emergent Reading / Shared Reading Skills about characters in stories. The second SFI sits in Term 1 ('Discusses and describes characters in stories'; LCs: describes characters in stories, discusses characters in stories), while the first sits in Term 3 ('Describes the characteristics of characters in stories or television and gives opinions'; LCs: describes the characteristics of characters in stories or television, gives opinions about characters in stories or television). This is not mere repetition: the Term 3 statement extends general describing/discussing to describing specific characteristics, widens the text base to television as well as stories, and adds evaluative response (giving opinions). Earlier-term competence in talking about and describing characters plausibly supports the later-term, more analytic and opinion-giving work, so the permitted within-grade direction is Term 1 to Term 3, i.e. second_to_first. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), so the judgment rests on the printed bullet text, identity scope and LCs supplied.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade 3 (rank 3), Term 4, Reading and Phonics Skills, but under different printed sub-strands: 'Shared Reading' (uses visual cues to read graphical texts; begins to analyse text for attitudes and assumptions, e.g. advertisements) and 'Paired/Independent Reading' (reads independently at a more complex level for enjoyment or information from magazines and comics, fiction and non-fiction, and books read in Shared Reading sessions). The coherence is substantive and pair-specific, not mere wording overlap: the independent-reading statement explicitly draws on Shared Reading sessions and on text types (magazines, comics) that depend on the visual/graphical reading addressed in the Shared Reading bullet, so they mutually reinforce reading across text types. However, they sit in the same Grade and same Term with no evidence that proficiency in one is developmentally prior to the other — one targets critical/visual text analysis in a teacher-led setting, the other breadth and independence of reading — so a same-rank, same-term developmental direction is not substantively supported. Endpoint source evidence for both SFIs is truncated (24 omitted items each) and both carry upstream audit/merge context, but the retained statement text is clear enough for a symmetric judgment.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade 2 Reading and Phonics > Daily Phonic Activities skills on weekly spelling. The second SFI sits in Grade 2 Term 1 ('Learns to spell ten words a week taken from phonics lessons'), while the first sits in Grade 2 Term 3 and extends the same weekly ten-word spelling routine to words 'taken from phonics lessons and sight words'. This is a pair-specific broadening of the word source (phonics-derived words plus sight vocabulary) later in the same grade, not mere repeated wording, so Term 1 proficiency supports success in the Term 3 statement. Within-grade direction therefore runs earlier term to later term (second_to_first); both endpoints are resolved at Grade 2 rank 2 with source-backed Term scope, though each endpoint's source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items per SFI), which limits confirmation beyond the printed statement text.

judgment.rationale: 'Builds words using sounds learnt' (Grade 1, rank 1 / Term 4 / Reading and Phonics / Daily Phonic Activities, Phonics sub-strand) and 'Writes words using sounds learnt' (Grade 1, rank 1 / Term 2 / Writing / Shared, Group and Independent Writing) both require learners to apply already-taught letter-sound knowledge to construct whole words, one through phonics word-building activity and one through encoding in independent writing. The shared LC tags 'phonics' and 'sounds' and the two sub-strand contexts support real, pair-specific instructional coherence between decoding/encoding practice in the phonics programme and applying the same sounds when writing words, so this is meaningful complementary reinforcement rather than generic repeated wording. A developmental claim is not supported: the statements are near-identical parallel bullets in different skill areas, the Term 4 phonics context ('Introduce new consonant blends. Continue word building and aural recognition activities.') describes an ongoing recurrent phonics activity rather than an extension of the Term 2 writing skill, and the earlier-term/later-term ordering of these two printed instances is incidental to where each bullet happens to appear. Because no pair-specific increase in capability is evidenced in either direction, the symmetric relatesTo (null direction, canonical endpoint order preserved) is the correct complete judgment. Confidence is moderate because both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all endpoints and ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills are co-located bullets in the same Grade 1 / Term 2 / Writing / 'Shared, Group and Independent Writing' table row (page 70, window 19), with identical coordinate rank (Grade 1) and the same term, so no grade- or term-based developmental ordering is available. Substantively they are complementary emergent-writing tasks: 'Draws pictures to convey a message, adding a label or caption' (LCs: drawing to convey a message; adding a label or caption to a drawing) and 'Compiles a list of words according to instructions such as food' (LC tags: instructions, vocabulary, word list). Both require producing words in writing to serve a communicative purpose, so they reinforce each other, but nothing in the bounded evidence establishes that proficiency in one is needed for or materially supports success in the other rather than them being parallel same-term activities; the only cross-signals are the generic shared 'writing' LC tag and stopword/trigram overlap, which alone do not establish direction. relatesTo therefore fits better than a developmental edge. Note that source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each) and LC evidence for the first endpoint is truncated, so finer-grained sequencing evidence may exist outside this excerpt.
